import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 141

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture141

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 141](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`,
`tree(G) ≥ ⌊girth(G) / 2⌋ - 1 + max_v l(v)`
where `tree(G)` is the number of vertices of a largest induced tree subgraph,
`girth(G)` is the length of the shortest cycle (0 if acyclic), and
`l(v) = indepNeighbors G v` is the independence number of the neighbourhood of `v`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture141 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    (G.girth / 2 : ℤ) - 1 + ((Finset.univ.sup (indepNeighborsCard G) : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤
    (largestInducedTreeSize G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `largestInducedTreeSize` invariant is a natural number (nonneg). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ largestInducedTreeSize G := Nat.zero_le _

/-- The path graph `P₃` has 3 vertices; `n P₃ = 3`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : Fintype.card (Fin 3) = 3 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture141

findings.description: Line 43 uses integer division: `(G.girth / 2 : ℤ)` elaborates as `(G.girth : ℤ) / 2`, hence equals ⌊girth(G)/2⌋. The source does not round down. Writing L for the maximum local independence number and T for the largest induced tree size, the source's inequality is equivalent to T ≥ ⌈girth(G)/2⌉ − 1 + L, since T and L are integers. For odd girth 2k+1, Lean instead states T ≥ k−1+L rather than T ≥ k+L. The docstring repeats the same unsupported floor. The division semantics and the correct ceiling reformulation were verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaVina's Written on the Wall II, entry 141, dated July 19, 2005, states: “If G is a simple connected graph, then tree(G) ≥ (1/2)*girth − 1 + maximum of λ(v).” There is no floor. Read in the July 26, 2026 snapshot: http://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html . Its linked definitions identify tree(G) as the number of vertices in a largest induced tree and λ(v) as neighbourhood independence.
findings.suggested_fix: Use rational or real division and remove the floor from the docstring. Alternatively, the exact division-free statement is `G.girth + 2 * Finset.univ.sup (indepNeighborsCard G) ≤ 2 * (largestInducedTreeSize G + 1)`. This natural-number inequality was proved equivalent to the source's unrounded rational inequality in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Separately from the rounding defect, `[Nontrivial α]` excludes singleton graphs, although the source just says “simple connected graph.”
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A connected graph with at most one vertex is K₁. Under the file's zero-girth convention, it has girth 0, maximum local independence 0 and largest induced tree size 1; both the source and rounded inequalities hold automatically. Thus restricting to nontrivial vertex types loses no substantive case. The universal unrounded inequality with and without the Nontrivial restriction was proved equivalent in Lean.

sources_consulted: http://web.archive.org/web/20040328085621id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu:80/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html — earlier version consulted during source retrieval
FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/LargestInducedTree.lean and Independence.lean, at the reviewed checkout
Mathlib source at the reviewed checkout: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/{Girth,Clique,Acyclic,Paths,Maps,Connectivity/Connected}.lean and Data/Finset/Lattice/Fold.lean
review.notes: The live source's HTTPS endpoint timed out; the latest accessible all.html snapshot, July 26, 2026, still labels 141 O (open), so no status discrepancy was evidenced. The linked girth definition does not specify an acyclic value; zero was not treated as a defect, since the bound is automatic on connected acyclic graphs, as proved in the scratch file. Both anonymous test declarations are mathematically accurate. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors and checks the arithmetic, bounded finite maxima, singleton and acyclic cases, and computations for the empty graph, K₁, K₂, K₃, P₃, C₄, C₅ and C₇. The reviewed file was not modified.

submission.summary: Changed the inequality to rational arithmetic so half the girth is not rounded down, and removed the floor from the docstring. Left the hypotheses, attributes, references, and other declarations unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
